gaps.description: Establish whether differential partitioning can be connected to an internal RNA-poor compartment and measured f, and whether the conditional lever-rule signature is physically applicable. C1 computes phase-volume consequences but cannot identify cavity identity, causal effects in B, or an image-area mapping; an explicit equal-partition limit check is still needed.

variables_units.f: dimensionless arithmetic mean over droplets of segmented internal dark area / filled area
variables_units.C_ref,d,C_var,d,C_ref,l,C_var,l: ng/uL measured E04 endpoint concentrations in dense (d) and dilute (l) phases
variables_units.K_i: dimensionless dense/dilute concentration ratio C_i,d/C_i,l, undefined when C_i,l=0
variables_units.x_var: dimensionless variant fraction by RNA mass in the total mixture; hypothetical input, not known from DNA reads
variables_units.r: dimensionless global variant/reference RNA mass ratio x_var/(1-x_var)
variables_units.phi_l: dimensionless dilute-phase volume fraction; hypothetical and not the image-area statistic
variables_units.M_ref,M_var: ng total species masses, with M_i=V_d*C_i,d+V_l*C_i,l

equations: For species i, M_i=V_d*C_i,d+V_l*C_i,l (ng = uL * ng/uL).

Let phi_l=V_l/(V_d+V_l), delta_i=C_i,l-C_i,d, and r=M_var/M_ref. Then r=[C_var,d+phi_l*delta_var]/[C_ref,d+phi_l*delta_ref], hence phi_l=(C_var,d-r*C_ref,d)/(r*delta_ref-delta_var), when the denominator is nonzero and 0<=phi_l<=1. Equivalently x_var=M_var/(M_ref+M_var), so r=x_var/(1-x_var).
The lever rule requires fixed coexisting endpoint concentrations and no additional species or phase; endpoint data alone do not determine phi_l because r is unknown.
Measured image observable remains f=mean_j(A_internal,j/A_filled,j); no equality between f and phi_l is assumed.
parameters_ranges: C1 evaluated x_var=0,.1,...,1 for each E04 tie-line using central endpoints; only values with 0<=phi_l<=1 are compatible with that fixed tie-line.
C1 varied all 16 lower/upper marginal endpoint corners per tie-line at x_var=.1,...,.9; these are sensitivity envelopes, not statistical intervals.
Use E04 endpoint bounds only as reported; do not treat endpoints as B measurements or infer RNA mass fraction from DNA read frequencies.
Any phase-to-image geometry parameter or carryover effect remains unspecified and must be labeled hypothetical if introduced.
initial_boundary_conditions: C1 assumes a closed two-phase system, conserved reference and variant masses, fixed coexisting endpoints and no third component, source, sink or exchange during lever-rule evaluation.
No actual initial amounts, phase volumes, RNA production composition or boundary fluxes are supplied.
C1 handles pure-species endpoints as underdetermined for phase volume; the equal-partition limit has not yet been explicitly computed and should be checked.
observation_mapping: E01 f is an image-derived area statistic, not concentration, volume fraction or free energy.
E02 is endpoint imaging of gel-purified template length fractions, not direct RNA species concentration or mixture mass fraction.
E04 is measured coexisting-phase endpoint concentration data; it is not B time-course, cavity-local sampling or phase-volume data.
C1 predicts conditional phi_l only and provides no mapping from phi_l to f.

A discriminating future observation would quantify RNA species mass fractions in internal and outer/dilute regions and f in matched droplets/preparations over time, while holding age, total RNA and carryover fixed.
alternatives: H2: age/carryover-driven cavitation without variant enrichment; predicts no necessary composition-linked species enrichment after matching age and carryover.
Population composition, droplet selection, segmentation or changing filled-area denominators can alter aggregate f without within-droplet phase growth.
predictions: Conditional H1: if an E04-like tie-line applies, independently measured x_var must lie in its compatible range and determines phi_l; the tie-line-specific species concentrations predict which RNA is enriched in each phase. Tie-line 1 and tie-line 2 imply opposite relative variant/reference dense-phase preferences.
H2: at matched age, total RNA and carryover, changing x_var alone need not produce tie-line-specific species enrichment or phase-volume response.
A matched composition series measuring internal-phase species enrichment and f distinguishes these accounts; absence of enrichment weakens H1, while f alone does not identify it.
No 36/48 h time extrapolation is committed.
checks: C1 units check passes: uL*ng/uL=ng; r, x_var and phi_l are dimensionless.
C1 reconstructs both normalized species mass fractions at valid central points with residuals approximately 0 to 2.3e-15.
Zero dilute concentration makes K undefined; C1 reports tie-line 0 variant ratio undefined rather than zero or infinity.
C1 flags central and corner solutions outside [0,1] as incompatible rather than clipping; pure-species endpoints are underdetermined without total concentration.
Explicit equal-partition synthetic limit and denominator-degenerate test are not included in C1 output; request a focused check before accepting the derivation as complete.
Do not equate phase volume to cross-sectional area or f without geometry, sampling and segmentation assumptions.
Keep preparation-level replication separate from field/object summaries.
evidence_conflicts: At tie-line 1, variant dense/dilute ratio is much larger than reference's; at tie-line 2, it is smaller. Thus the relative partition preference varies across measured states and does not support universal variant enrichment in a dilute/internal phase.
Tie-line 0 variant is absent in both phases, so it cannot define variant partition preference or mixed-composition behavior.
E02 endpoint differences are compatible with composition effects but do not isolate composition from preparation, RNA yield or carryover.
E04 marginal uncertainty is broad and does not establish morphology, cavity identity, B composition or causality.
untested: Whether observed DNA variants are transcribed and their RNA mass fractions.
Whether those RNAs correspond to the E04 variant or E02 length classes.
Whether cavities are a dilute liquid phase or which compartment they represent.
Whether phase volume, geometry and persistence determine segmented f.
Whether age/carryover or composition is causal in B.

request.purpose: Compute the conditional lever-rule map from assumed total variant RNA mass fraction to dilute-phase volume fraction for each supplied E04 tie-line; quantify how the result changes across endpoint marginal-error corners and compare the relative partition ratios. x_var is a hypothetical independently measured RNA mass fraction; DNA read fractions are not RNA fractions.
Supplied marginal lower/upper endpoint bounds are varied as corners for sensitivity only; do not call them confidence intervals.

model_spec.range_conditions: For each tie_line_id 0,1,2, evaluate x_var=0,0.1,...,1.0. Compute phi_l=(C_var,d-r*C_ref,d)/(r*(C_ref,l-C_ref,d)-(C_var,l-C_var,d)), r=x_var/(1-x_var); handle x_var=1 with the species-only limit. Retain only values in [0,1] as lever-rule-compatible; flag invalid values. Recompute at all combinations of lower/upper supplied endpoint bounds (16 corners per tie-line), skipping undefined K ratios when a dilute concentration is zero. Include central endpoint K_ref,K_var and K_var/K_ref where defined. Report residual reconstruction of normalized masses for valid points, equal-partition/zero-species/degenerate checks, and whether relative preference direction differs across tie-lines.
